You are reviewing the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim (branch llamacpp) for STRUCTURAL refactor candidates.
First read /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md to understand the architecture.

HARD RULES:
- READ-ONLY. Do not edit, build, or run anything (no make, no scripts, no ./andesim). Baseline test runs are using the build tree right now. Use Read/Grep/Glob and read-only git commands only.
- Structural = behavior-preserving: dead code, duplication, needless complexity, stale comments/docs that contradict the code, naming that hides intent, repo hygiene. NOT rewrites for taste. The repo just went through a history cleanup, so it is fairly clean; report only what you can defend with evidence. An empty findings list is a valid answer.
- If you find what looks like a real BUG (behavior wrong), report it with category "bug-report" - it will be handled separately, not as a refactor.
- For every finding give: file (repo-relative), line, category, title, one-paragraph detail with EVIDENCE (what you read/grepped), safety (why removing/changing it cannot change behavior), verify_with (which existing test or check proves it after the change).
- Cite real file paths and line numbers you actually read. No speculation.

Your assigned scope (do not wander into other subsystems except to grep for references):
tests/e2e.sh, tests/lib/ (helpers), tests/andes_sim/*.sh, tests/plugin/*.sh, tests/vplat/*.sh, and scripts/run_e2e.sh interplay. Copy-paste across the ~30 contract scripts (arg parsing, assert helpers, setup boilerplate) that tests/lib should own; dead test scripts referencing removed features.

Return your findings as the structured output.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.

Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). 4	# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap

13	#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
14	#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
15	#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
16	#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
17	#                   relies on this; ./andesim run always passes them explicitly.
18	#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
19	#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
20	#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
21	#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
22	#   CHECK_PRIV=<0|1|3>         assert both drained state files carry this
23	#                              privilege (L6: 0=U, 1=S, 3=M).
24	#   CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=<re>     assert the vsim leg's output (guest UART rides

94	# 128 MB program RAM matches the QEMU virt machine default. L26/F2: the

120	# LM/HVM content transport (ROADMAP_ilm_dlm, ROADMAP_hvm): mirror the
121	# driver's run_plan wiring. The engine's --describe reports its memories in
122	# BYTES; when a size is > 0 the QEMU plugin drains that memory's content to
123	# a sidecar next to the state file and the vsim leg backdoor-loads it
124	# (--ilm/--dlm/--hvm). An engine without the memory (or an older binary
125	# whose --describe lacks the field) adds nothing. ILM_SIZE/DLM_SIZE/HVM_SIZE
126	# env override the probe; 0 forces that memory's transport off
127	# (negative-control knob).
128	#
129	# QEMU's memory GEOMETRY is synced separately and ALWAYS (lm_geom, from the
130	# engine's describe -- the raw analog of the driver's
131	# --print-qemu-config/-readconfig sync), so a transport-off negative still
132	# runs the guest against the engine's real geometry. This matters twice:
133	# QEMU's compiled-in ILM default is 2 MB at 0x0, which SHADOWS the program
134	# image at 0x100000 the moment a guest sets milmb.EN (the engine's real
135	# 64 KB ends at 0xFFFF); and QEMU's HVM default is 1 BYTE
136	# (hvm_size_pow_2=0), which would fault an HVM fixture's fill outright.
137	# Probe the engine's real sizes ONCE; lm_geom always uses these, while the
138	# *_SIZE transport knobs default to them but may be overridden (0 = the
139	# negative-control off switch).
140	ILM_REAL=$(hybrid_describe_int ilm_size)
141	DLM_REAL=$(hybrid_describe_int dlm_size)
142	HVM_REAL=$(hybrid_describe_int hvm_size)
143	ILM_SIZE="${ILM_SIZE:-$ILM_REAL}"
144	DLM_SIZE="${DLM_SIZE:-$DLM_REAL}"
145	HVM_SIZE="${HVM_SIZE:-$HVM_REAL}"
146	VSIM_LM_ARGS=()
147	QEMU_LM_ARGS=()
148	lm_geom() {  # $1 ilm|dlm|hvm, $2 engine bytes ("" or 0 = engine has none)
149	  [ -n "$2" ] && [ "$2" -gt 0 ] || return 0
150	  if [ "$1" = hvm ]; then
151	    # QEMU's HVM geometry property is a power of two, not bytes.
152	    local p=0 v=$2
153	    while [ "$v" -gt 1 ]; do v=$((v >> 1)); p=$((p + 1)); done
154	    QEMU_LM_ARGS+=(-global "driver=riscv.andes.ae350.soc,property=hvm_size_pow_2,value=$p")
155	  else
156	    QEMU_LM_ARGS+=(-global "driver=riscv.andes.ae350.soc,property=$1_size,value=$2")
157	  fi
158	}
159	lm_wire() {  # $1 ilm|dlm|hvm, $2 size in bytes ("" or 0 = transport off)
160	  [ -n "$2" ] && [ "$2" -gt 0 ] || return 0
161	  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,$1_size=$2"
162	  VSIM_LM_ARGS+=("--$1" "$STATE_QEMU.$1")
163	}

165	lm_geom dlm "$DLM_REAL"
166	lm_geom hvm "$HVM_REAL"

168	lm_wire dlm "$DLM_SIZE"

175	# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
176	# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim has no separate "roi"
177	# flag -- its hybrid leg only ever executes the ROI (resumes at the
178	# boundary, exits on the trigger), so plain --kanata already covers

188	echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"

204

207	  exit 1
208	fi
209	
210	if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
211	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
212	  exit 1
213	fi
214	
215	echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
216	set +e
217	timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
218	  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
219	  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
220	  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
221	  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
222	  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
223	  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
224	  "${VSIM_LM_ARGS[@]}" \
225	  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
226	VSIM_RC=$?
227	set -e
228	
229	# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
230	# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
231	# drained cleanly.
232	if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
233	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
234	  echo "--- sim log ---"
235	  cat "$SIM_LOG"
236	  exit 1
237	fi
238	
239	# LM/HVM exit-dump check: vsim dumps its ILM/DLM/HVM content next to the
240	# handoff-out state file; for a ROI that never writes those memories, the
241	# exit bytes must equal the entry bytes -- one byte-exact loop through
242	# plugin drain -> sidecar -> backdoor load -> RTL SRAM -> exit dump.
243	if [ "${CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS:-0}" = "1" ]; then
244	  for pair in "ilm:${ILM_SIZE:-0}" "dlm:${DLM_SIZE:-0}" "hvm:${HVM_SIZE:-0}"; do
245	    kind="${pair%%:*}"; sz="${pair##*:}"
246	    [ -n "$sz" ] && [ "$sz" -gt 0 ] || continue
247	    if [ ! -f "$STATE_VSIM.$kind" ]; then
248	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim did not dump $STATE_VSIM.$kind at exit"
249	      exit 1
250	    fi
251	    if ! cmp -s "$STATE_QEMU.$kind" "$STATE_VSIM.$kind"; then
252	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: $kind exit content differs from entry content:"
253	      cmp "$STATE_QEMU.$kind" "$STATE_VSIM.$kind" | head -3
254	      exit 1
255	    fi
256	  done
257	  echo "[$FIXTURE lm-exit] PASS: exit LM/HVM content matches entry byte-for-byte"
258	fi
259	
260	# In-ROI verdict check: the guest printed its result on the vsim leg's UART.
261	if [ -n "${CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT:-}" ]; then
262	  if grep -qE "$CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT" "$SIM_LOG"; then
263	    echo "[$FIXTURE vsim-stdout] PASS: matched '$CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT'"
264	  else
265	    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim output did not match '$CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT'"
266	    echo "--- sim log (tail) ---"
267	    tail -25 "$SIM_LOG"
268	    exit 1
269	  fi
270	fi
271	
272	# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
273	# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
274	# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
275	# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
276	# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
277	read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
278	if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
279	  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
280	  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
281	  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
282	  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
283	  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
284	  # L6: privilege survives the handoff. priv@24 locked by state_abi_check.h.
285	  if [ -n "${CHECK_PRIV:-}" ]; then
286	    Q1_PRIV=$(read_u64_le 24 "$STATE_QEMU")
287	    V_PRIV=$(read_u64_le  24 "$STATE_VSIM")
288	    echo "[$FIXTURE priv] qemu1=$Q1_PRIV vsim=$V_PRIV expected=$CHECK_PRIV"
289	    if [ "$Q1_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ] || [ "$V_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ]; then
290	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: drained priv mismatch (expected $CHECK_PRIV)"
291	      exit 1
292	    fi
293	  fi
294	  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
295	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
296	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
297	    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
298	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
299	      exit 1
300	    fi
301	    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
302	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
303	      exit 1
304	    fi
305	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
306	  fi
307	fi
308	
309	echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"

161	# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
162	# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
163	# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
164	# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
165	# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
166	# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
167	# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
168	run_one() {
169	  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
170	  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
171	  local start end elapsed status rc
172	  start=$(date +%s)
173	  set +e
174	  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
175	  rc=$?
176	  set -e
177	  end=$(date +%s)
178	  elapsed=$((end - start))
179	  case $rc in
180	    0)  status=PASS ;;
181	    77) status=SKIP ;;
182	    *)  status=FAIL ;;
183	  esac
184	  (
185	    flock 9
186	    case "$status" in
187	      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
188	      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
189	      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
190	    esac
191	    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
192	      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
193	  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
194	}

196	# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
197	# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
198	# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
199	declare -a WORKPLAN=()
200	for tm in marker pc; do
201	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
202	  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
203	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
204	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
205	    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
206	    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
207	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
208	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
209	    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
210	  done
211	done
212	for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
213	  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
214	  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
215	  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
216	  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
217	done
218	
219	# Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
220	# after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
221	declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
222	for tm in marker pc; do
223	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
224	  for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
225	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
226	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
227	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
228	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
229	    SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
230	  done
231	done
232	
233	TOTAL=$(( ${#WORKPLAN[@]} + ${#SERIAL_PLAN[@]} ))
234	step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"
235	
236	# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
237	# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
238	# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
239	# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
240	# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
241	# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
242	SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
243	mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
244	exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
245	rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
246	for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
247	  printf '.\n' >&8
248	done
249	
250	i=0
251	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
252	  i=$((i+1))
253	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
254	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
255	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
256	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
257	  read -r -u 8 _tok
258	  (
259	    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
260	    printf '.\n' >&8
261	  ) &
262	done
263	wait
264	exec 8>&-
265	
266	# Serial phase: each heavyweight test gets the machine to itself.
267	for w in "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
268	  i=$((i+1))
269	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
270	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
271	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
272	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
273	  run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
274	done
275	
276	declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
277	declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
278	declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
279	declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
280	while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
281	  case "$r_status" in
282	    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
283	    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
284	    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
285	          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
286	  esac
287	done < "$RESULTS_FILE"
288	
289	# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
290	# deterministic post-run failure dump.
291	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}" "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
292	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
293	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
294	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
295	  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
296	                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
297	  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
298	    echo
299	    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
300	    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
301	  fi
302	done
303	
304	echo
305	marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
306	pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
307	neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
308	total_pass=$((marker_p + pc_p + neg_p))
309	total_fail=$((marker_f + pc_f + neg_f))
310	total_skip=$((marker_s + pc_s + neg_s))
311	step "summary: marker ${marker_p}p/${marker_f}f/${marker_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
312	if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
313	  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
314	  exit 1
315	fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ROI boundary resolution for pc-trigger mode.
3	#
4	# pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs: the ROI start (drain QEMU) and
5	# the ROI end (drain vsim). Either boundary may be named as a 0x-prefixed
6	# hex address (used verbatim) OR as a symbol present in the ELF (resolved
7	# against `nm --defined-only` output). This decouples the switch points from
8	# the workload source: any function can be the ROI, with no planted markers.
9	
10	# resolve_pc <boundary> <nm_output>
11	#   <boundary>  : "0x<hex>" | "0X<hex>" | symbol name
12	#   <nm_output> : `nm --defined-only` listing ("addr type name" per line)
13	# Prints the bare hex address (no 0x) on stdout, or nothing if a symbol name
14	# is not found (the caller treats empty as a fatal "cannot resolve").
15	resolve_pc() {
16	  local boundary="$1" nm_out="$2"
17	  case "$boundary" in
18	    0x*|0X*) printf '%s\n' "${boundary#0[xX]}" ;;
19	    *)       printf '%s\n' "$nm_out" | awk -v s="$boundary" '$3==s{print $1; exit}' ;;
20	  esac
21	}
22	
23	# roi_resolve_pair <nm_output> [<label>]
24	#   Reads ROI_START / ROI_END from the environment (both REQUIRED), resolves
25	#   each against <nm_output>, and sets the globals ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC (bare
26	#   hex). Returns 1 and prints a FAIL line naming the offending boundary if
27	#   either is unset or does not resolve. <label> tags the FAIL message.
28	roi_resolve_pair() {
29	  local nm_out="$1" label="${2:-pc}"
30	  local start="${ROI_START:-}"
31	  local end="${ROI_END:-}"
32	  if [ -z "$start" ] || [ -z "$end" ]; then
33	    echo "FAIL[$label]: ROI_START and ROI_END must both be set (0x address or symbol name)"
34	    return 1
35	  fi
36	  ENTER_PC=$(resolve_pc "$start" "$nm_out")
37	  EXIT_PC=$(resolve_pc "$end" "$nm_out")
38	  if [ -z "$ENTER_PC" ]; then
39	    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI start '$start' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
40	    return 1
41	  fi
42	  if [ -z "$EXIT_PC" ]; then
43	    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI end '$end' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
44	    return 1
45	  fi
46	  return 0
47	}
48	
49	# roi_markers_from_disasm <objdump_disasm>
50	#   Derives the two pc-mode switch PCs from the ROI marker HINTs a fixture
51	#   embeds, scanning `objdump -d` text:
52	#     ENTER = the entry marker     `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`  (encoding 5a002013)
53	#     EXIT  = the LAST exit marker `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`  (encoding 5a102013)
54	#   Both are the marker PCs themselves: the plugin (enter_pc=) and vsim
55	#   (--hybrid-exit-pc) each resume one insn past the trigger
56	#   (compute_handoff_pc = vaddr+size), so feeding the marker PC reproduces
57	#   marker mode's switch points exactly -- no offset arithmetic here. EXIT
58	#   keeps the LAST marker so a fixture that jumps over poison exit-marker
59	#   padding (rt_pc_jump) resolves to the real, reachable exit, not the first
60	#   dead one. The raw-bytes match is mnemonic-independent, so no objdump
61	#   decode table is needed.
62	#   Prints "ENTER EXIT" as bare hex; returns 1 (prints nothing) if either
63	#   marker is absent. This lets the bulk runner drive pc mode with no
64	#   per-fixture config; ./andesim run still passes explicit boundaries.
65	roi_markers_from_disasm() {
66	  printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '
67	    $2 == "5a002013" && enter == "" { e = $1; sub(/:$/, "", e); enter = e }
68	    $2 == "5a102013"                { x = $1; sub(/:$/, "", x); exit_pc = x }
69	    END {
70	      if (enter != "" && exit_pc != "") { print enter, exit_pc }
71	      else                              { exit 1 }
72	    }
73	  '
74	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# RED->GREEN: resolve_pc maps an ROI boundary (a symbol name OR a 0x-hex
3	# address) to a bare hex address, resolving symbols against `nm` output.
4	# This is the primitive that lets pc mode point at ANY symbol/address
5	# instead of the planted _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc markers.
6	set -uo pipefail
7	
8	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
9	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/roi.sh"
10	
11	fail() { echo "FAIL[roi_resolve]: $1"; exit 1; }
12	
13	# Fake `nm --defined-only` output (columns: addr type name).
14	NM_FIXTURE='0000000000100002 T _hybrid_enter_pc
15	0000000000100020 T _hybrid_exit_pc
16	0000000000100040 T vmatmul_kernel
17	0000000000100000 T main'
18	
19	# 1. hex passthrough strips the 0x prefix, keeps the digits.
20	got=$(resolve_pc "0x100abc" "$NM_FIXTURE")
21	[ "$got" = "100abc" ] || fail "hex passthrough: want 100abc got '$got'"
22	
23	# 2. uppercase 0X prefix also stripped.
24	got=$(resolve_pc "0X1f" "$NM_FIXTURE")
25	[ "$got" = "1f" ] || fail "0X prefix: want 1f got '$got'"
26	
27	# 3. arbitrary symbol name resolves via nm output.
28	got=$(resolve_pc "vmatmul_kernel" "$NM_FIXTURE")
29	[ "$got" = "0000000000100040" ] || fail "symbol resolve: want ...100040 got '$got'"
30	
31	# 4. unknown symbol -> empty (caller turns this into a FAIL).
32	got=$(resolve_pc "nope" "$NM_FIXTURE")
33	[ -z "$got" ] || fail "unknown symbol: want empty got '$got'"
34	
35	# --- roi_resolve_pair: env-required + dual resolve, as e2e.sh uses it ---
36	
37	# 5. unset ROI_START/ROI_END -> error (no implicit fallback).
38	unset ROI_START ROI_END
39	out=$(roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" t 2>&1)
40	[ $? -ne 0 ] || fail "unset pair: expected nonzero return"
41	case "$out" in *"ROI_START and ROI_END"*) ;; *) fail "unset pair: missing required-vars message: '$out'";; esac
42	
43	# 6. ROI_START symbol + ROI_END hex resolve to ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC.
44	ROI_START=vmatmul_kernel ROI_END=0x100100 roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" t \
45	  || fail "override pair: returned nonzero"
46	[ "$ENTER_PC" = "0000000000100040" ] || fail "ENTER_PC: got '$ENTER_PC'"
47	[ "$EXIT_PC"  = "100100" ]            || fail "EXIT_PC: got '$EXIT_PC'"
48	
49	# 7. an unresolvable boundary fails loudly and names the offender.
50	out=$(ROI_START=ghost ROI_END=main roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" myfix 2>&1)
51	[ $? -ne 0 ] || fail "bad start: expected nonzero return"
52	case "$out" in *"myfix"*"ghost"*) ;; *) fail "bad start: message missing label/symbol: '$out'";; esac
53	
54	# --- roi_markers_from_disasm: derive pc-mode boundaries from ROI markers ----
55	# Lets the bulk runner drive pc mode with no per-fixture config: ENTER is the
56	# entry marker `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (enc 5a002013), EXIT is the LAST exit
57	# marker `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (enc 5a102013). Both are the marker PCs -- the
58	# plugin/vsim resume one insn past the trigger (compute_handoff_pc=vaddr+size),
59	# reproducing marker mode's switch points. Inputs are `objdump -d` fragments.
60	
61	# 8. in-order fixture: entry marker -> single exit marker.
62	DISASM_INORDER='  10023c: 5a002013  slti zero,zero,1440
63	  100240: 5a102013  slti zero,zero,1441
64	  100244: 8082  ret'
65	got=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$DISASM_INORDER") \
66	  || fail "in-order: function returned nonzero"
67	[ "$got" = "10023c 100240" ] || fail "in-order: want '10023c 100240' got '$got'"
68	
69	# 9. jump-over-poison fixture (rt_pc_jump): the c.j skips dead exit markers;
70	#    the LAST 5a102013 is the real, reachable exit -- not the first.
71	DISASM_JUMP='  100000: 5a002013  slti zero,zero,1440
72	  100004: a83d  c.j 0x100042
73	  100006: 5a102013  slti zero,zero,1441
74	  10000a: 5a102013  slti zero,zero,1441
75	  100042: 5a102013  slti zero,zero,1441
76	  100046: 4601  c.li a2,0'
77	got=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$DISASM_JUMP") \
78	  || fail "jump: function returned nonzero"
79	[ "$got" = "100000 100042" ] || fail "jump: want '100000 100042' (last exit) got '$got'"
80	
81	# 10. no markers -> nonzero return, empty output.
82	DISASM_NONE='  100000: 1141  c.addi sp,sp,-16
83	  100002: 8082  ret'
84	got=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$DISASM_NONE"); rc=$?
85	[ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || fail "no-markers: expected nonzero return, got rc=0"
86	[ -z "$got" ]   || fail "no-markers: expected empty output, got '$got'"
87	
88	echo "[roi_resolve] PASS"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# F4 contract: HTIF file syscalls behave identically on both engines. The
3	# SAME vplat_file.elf creates/writes/reads/removes a host file (served by
4	# vsim's sim_control HTIF table and by QEMU's andes_sim_control mirror),
5	# prints "file io ok" and exits 0. Run in a scratch cwd; the tmp file must
6	# be gone afterwards (remove() worked host-side).
7	set -uo pipefail
8	
9	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
10	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
11	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
12	
13	# shellcheck disable=SC1091
14	. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
15	export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"
16	
17	ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_file.elf"
18	SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
19	QEMU="${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv64"
20	[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"
21	[ -x "$QEMU" ] || fail "qemu not found (source ./setup.sh): $QEMU"
22	
23	make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_file.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"
24	
25	run_leg() {  # LABEL CMD...
26	  local label="$1"; shift
27	  local wd out rc
28	  wd=$(mktemp -d)
29	  out=$( cd "$wd" && timeout 120 "$@" </dev/null 2>&1 ); rc=$?
30	  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'file io ok' \
31	    || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: missing 'file io ok': $out"; }
32	  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: exit code $rc != 0"; }
33	  [ ! -e "$wd/vplat_file_test.tmp" ] \
34	    || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: tmp file not removed"; }
35	  rm -rf "$wd"
36	  echo "[ok] $label: file io ok, clean exit, tmp removed"
37	}
38	
39	run_leg cycle "$SIM" "$ELF"
40	run_leg fast "$QEMU" -machine andes_ae350 -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
41	  -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native -bios "$ELF"
42	
43	# rv32 leg (guarded): on rv32 the tohost command reaches the device as TWO
44	# 32-bit halves (0x10 low, 0x14 high) instead of one 64-bit store, so it
45	# exercises a distinct device path. Skips when the rv32 toolchain, runtime,
46	# or qemu-system-riscv32 is absent.
47	QEMU32="${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv32"
48	GCC32="$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc"
49	if [ -x "$QEMU32" ] && [ -x "$GCC32" ] && [ -d "$ROOT/build/runtime/rv32" ]; then
50	  ELF32=$(mktemp -t vplat_file32.XXXXXX.elf)
51	  "$GCC32" -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -B "$ROOT/build/runtime/rv32" \
52	    -specs=andesim.specs "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_file.c" -o "$ELF32" \
53	    || fail "rv32 fixture build failed"
54	  run_leg fast-rv32 "$QEMU32" -machine andes_ae350 -cpu andes-a45 \
55	    -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native -bios "$ELF32"
56	  rm -f "$ELF32"
57	else
58	  echo "[skip] fast-rv32 leg: rv32 toolchain/runtime/qemu not available"
59	fi
